messages:
ellie_support: Heads-up — RavenCorp is hitting 429s from their Dedicated pool (quiet-pool-7) right after we applied their plan change at ~09:12 UTC. Customer says it started immediately after upgrade.

maya_cs: Oof. Customer reports >95% of generation calls returning 429s, response body: `{"error":"rate_limited","code":429,"detail":"per-tenant rate cap exceeded"}`. Impact: internal search + chat widgets.

matt_engineering: Can you paste the tenant rate_profile? My hunch: units/denominator mismatch or window misinterpretation after the plan swap.

ellie_support: Pasted the snippet they gave from admin: ```json
{"tenant":"ravencorp","rate_profile":{"rate_units":100,"rate_window":"60m","burst_cap":200}}
```

matt_engineering: There it is — `rate_units:100` with `rate_window:60m`. Previously their plan used per-minute units. Admin UI treats `rate_window` as minutes, but the new plan migration code wrote a literal string (60m) into a field expected as an integer number of minutes. So the runtime interpreted `60m` as 60 minutes *and* multiplied incorrectly when converting to internal tokens-per-second. Basically double-scaling causing effective cap to drop by ~60x during enforcement.

ops-bot: [alert] dedicated-pool-quiet-pool-7: spike in 429s (start 2026-03-17T09:12:46Z).

reza_infra: I can push a targeted fix to the tenant record (convert rate_window -> 60). Quick mitigation: set `rate_window` to `1` and scale `rate_units` accordingly so we maintain the same throughput. Example admin patch: ```bash
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://admin.internal/tenants/ravencorp \n  -d '{"rate_profile":{"rate_units":6000,"rate_window":1}}'
```

matt_engineering: Nice. Before we patch, can someone run a simulated load against a canary in quiet-pool-7 to reproduce? Use a small script hitting the customer route at their typical qps (8-10 r/s) and observe `x-rate-remaining` header and 429s.

reza_infra: Running now from infra-canary (quick script):
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $RAVEN_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate; sleep 0.1; done
```
Before patch: first 12 responses `200`, then 38x `429`. Response header sample: `x-rate-limit: 100/60m` and `x-rate-remaining: 0`.

reza_infra: Pushed patch to admin and purged tenant config cache:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.internal/tenants/ravencorp/purge-cache
```
After patch: rerunning load -> 50/50 `200`, `x-rate-limit: 6000/1m`, `x-rate-remaining` ~5948. No 429s.

ellie_support: Thanks — I'll update RavenCorp: "We've identified a migration bug that wrote a minute-window as a literal string; we've corrected your tenant rate profile and purged config caches. Expect traffic to resume immediately — we'll monitor for 2 hours and follow up." :white_check_mark:

maya_cs: Customer replied: "traffic is back, thanks" and sent logs showing normal latency. Marking as customer-resolved but keeping monitoring window open.

matt_engineering: Filed a tiny migration hotfix PR to validate `rate_window` parsing and add defensive validation on tenant writes. Link: internal-git/rate-migrations/PR-842. Will roll to staging canary tonight.

reza_infra: Added a short alert rule to detect sudden drops in `x-rate-limit` magnitude (>=10x) per-tenant and auto-flag to #eng-infra so we catch similar miswrites.

ellie_support: Great. Closing thread once 2h monitor passes. Thanks y'all. :raised_hands:
